items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Well, some piece of Duke’s with Milt Hinton, and Duke was very complimentary.

ctx.x: And somehow I… somehow that didn’t seem right to me. (laughs) I forgot how I got into that. Anyway, and I love Duke Ellington. Then I found out… oh, and I noticed that none of the, of Duke’s band were at the thing except Freddie Green, who had played guitar with Duke a hundred years ago. And a few months later, I was talking to, doing an interview with a woman who had known Duke Ellington really well. I think he was still alive. And she said that, that Duke hated Nixon so much that he booked another job for his…
We got in it because we were talking about Gerry Mulligan.

items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: There was five piano players, you remember? Five piano players. Willie “The Lion”, Earl Hines, Marian McPartland, and Hank Jones. And the drummer was Louie Bellson. Jim Hall was the guitar player—

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, friends of Ellington. Yeah.
There was five piano players, you remember? Five piano players. Willie “The Lion”, Earl Hines, Marian McPartland, and Hank Jones. And the drummer was Louie Bellson. Jim Hall was the guitar player—
And Dizzy Gillespie was just in the audience.
